label: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology
blurb: A focused six-fact drill set for Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology.

topics.title: Satellite
topics.hook: An artificial satellite orbits a larger body and can support communication, navigation, or observation.
topics.explainer: An artificial satellite orbits a larger body and can support communication, navigation, or observation. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology

connections.fact: A satellite placed over the equator with a 24-hour period appears fixed and is called geostationary.
GPS determines position from timing signals broadcast by multiple orbiting satellites.

topics.title: Geostationary orbit
topics.hook: A geostationary satellite appears fixed above Earth's equator because its period matches Earth's rotation.
topics.explainer: A geostationary satellite appears fixed above Earth's equator because its period matches Earth's rotation. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology

connections.relationship: Orbit that fixes apparent sky position
connections.fact: A satellite in this equatorial orbit matches Earth's rotation and appears stationary to a ground observer.

connections.relationship: Different orbit choices for different services
connections.fact: GPS satellites use medium Earth orbit rather than geostationary orbit, enabling worldwide navigation coverage.

topics.title: GPS
topics.hook: The Global Positioning System is a satellite-based navigation system operated by the United States.
topics.explainer: The Global Positioning System is a satellite-based navigation system operated by the United States. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology

connections.fact: A GPS receiver calculates position from precisely timed transmissions sent by a satellite constellation.
Many drones use GPS for position holding, route following, and return-to-home functions.

topics.title: Chandrayaan-3
topics.hook: Chandrayaan-3 achieved India's first successful soft landing on the Moon in 2023.
topics.explainer: Chandrayaan-3 achieved India's first successful soft landing on the Moon in 2023. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology

connections.fact: Chandrayaan-3 was an uncrewed lunar landing mission; Gaganyaan is intended to carry Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit.
Chandrayaan-3 used an orbiter-related propulsion module and lander-rover system, unlike routine communication or navigation satellites.

topics.title: Gaganyaan
topics.explainer: Gaganyaan is India's human-spaceflight programme. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology

connections.relationship: Human spaceflight contrasted with robotic exploration
connections.fact: Gaganyaan targets a crewed low-Earth-orbit flight, while Chandrayaan-3 placed robotic hardware on the Moon.

connections.relationship: Crew capsule and orbital spacecraft distinction
connections.fact: Both travel in space, but Gaganyaan is designed around safely carrying people rather than providing an unmanned satellite service.

topics.title: Drone
topics.hook: A drone is an unmanned aircraft controlled remotely or autonomously.
topics.explainer: A drone is an unmanned aircraft controlled remotely or autonomously. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Space, Satellites, Defence and Frontier Technology

connections.fact: GPS supplies location data that enables a drone to follow waypoints or return to its launch point.

connections.relationship: Aircraft in atmosphere versus spacecraft in orbit
connections.fact: A drone flies within Earth's atmosphere, whereas an artificial satellite remains in orbit around a larger body.

questions.q: Which object qualifies as an artificial satellite?
options: A human-made spacecraft orbiting Earth
A natural moon orbiting a planet
An unmanned aircraft flying in the atmosphere
A sounding rocket on a suborbital trajectory
questions.explanation: An artificial satellite remains in orbit around a larger body and may provide communication, observation, science, or navigation services.

questions.q: Why does a geostationary satellite appear fixed in the sky?
options: Its equatorial orbital period matches Earth’s rotation
Its polar orbit crosses the equator twice on every pass
Its orbital period is shorter than Earth’s rotation
It remains stationary without orbiting Earth
questions.explanation: A circular equatorial orbit with the same rotational period as Earth keeps the satellite over one longitude.

questions.q: Which country operates the Global Positioning System?
options: India
United States
France
Japan
questions.explanation: GPS is the United States satellite-navigation constellation; other systems include India's NavIC and Europe's Galileo.

options: India’s first successful lunar soft landing
India’s first Mars-orbit insertion
India’s first solar-observation orbit
India’s first crewed Earth-orbit mission
questions.explanation: The Vikram lander achieved India's first soft landing on the Moon and deployed the Pragyan rover.

questions.q: Which mission is designed as India's human-spaceflight programme?
options: Chandrayaan-3
Gaganyaan
Aditya-L1
Mangalyaan
questions.explanation: Gaganyaan is intended to carry an Indian crew to low Earth orbit and return them safely.

options: It is an unmanned aircraft controlled remotely or autonomously
It is a crewed aircraft flown only by an onboard pilot
It is an unpowered balloon tethered to the ground
It is a spacecraft maintained in Earth orbit
questions.explanation: A drone operates within the atmosphere without an onboard human pilot, using remote control, automation, or both.

options: Geostationary — fixed apparent position
GPS — satellite navigation
Drone — permanent Earth orbit
Satellite — communication or observation
questions.explanation: A drone is an aircraft in the atmosphere, not an orbital spacecraft; the other pairings describe standard space uses.

questions.q: A drone follows programmed waypoints and returns to its launch site. Which external system likely supplies position?
options: GPS
Inertial measurement unit
Visual odometry
Barometric altimeter
questions.explanation: Satellite-navigation fixes allow many drones to hold position, fly routes, and trigger return-to-home behaviour.

questions.q: Which comparison with Gaganyaan is accurate?
options: Chandrayaan-3 was robotic lunar exploration; Gaganyaan targets crewed Earth orbit
Both missions are designed to place crews on the lunar surface
Gaganyaan is a lunar rover while Chandrayaan-3 is an orbital crew capsule
Chandrayaan-3 and Gaganyaan are both satellite-navigation constellations
questions.explanation: The missions differ in destination and crew: Chandrayaan-3 was uncrewed and lunar, while Gaganyaan focuses on astronauts in low Earth orbit.

questions.q: Which navigation constellation is not geostationary?
options: GPS, whose satellites use medium Earth orbit
A fixed communications satellite over the equator
A weather satellite matching Earth's rotation
A broadcast spacecraft stationed over one longitude
questions.explanation: GPS satellites orbit in medium Earth orbit and move across the sky; geostationary satellites remain apparently fixed.
